stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Drag the source $S$ up and down along its rail. The rays fan out in straight lines from $S$ — the opaque bar cuts a sharp geometric shadow, and the whole shadow slides as $S$ moves.
stages.concept: Light propagates in straight lines. A point source at $S$ sends rays radially outward; any ray that meets an opaque object stops there, leaving a geometric shadow behind the object.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Three targets sit around the bar. Position $S$ so each target has a clear straight line to it, then press Fire (or Space). You have 5 shots to light all 3.
stages.concept: Target $T$ is illuminated iff the segment $ST$ misses the bar. The line $ST$ crosses the plane $x = O_x$ at height $y_{\text{hit}} = S_y + \frac{O_x - S_x}{T_x - S_x}\,(T_y - S_y)$; $T$ is lit when $y_{\text{hit}}$ falls outside the bar's vertical interval.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: Rays and shadow are hidden. Read the coordinates of $S$, of the bar, and of target $T$ from the scene. Compute $y_{\text{hit}} = S_y + \frac{O_x - S_x}{T_x - S_x}\,(T_y - S_y)$ on paper, set $S_y$ so $y_{\text{hit}}$ lies outside the bar, then Fire. One shot per target.
stages.concept: $y_{\text{hit}}$ is a linear interpolation between $S_y$ and $T_y$ evaluated at $x = O_x$. If $y_{\text{hit}} \in [O_{y1},\,O_{y2}]$ the ray is blocked and $T$ stays dark.

labels.exhausted: OUT OF SHOTS · RESET TO RETRY
labels.tip1: drag the source along its rail
labels.tip2: aim, then press SPACE to fire
labels.tip3: compute Sy from coordinates, then fire

1.1: Grab the orange source disk and drag it up or down. It slides along the dashed rail at x = 120.
1.2: Every ray from S is a straight line. The bar stops any ray that would cross it.
1.3: The dark cone behind the bar is the shadow — the set of points no straight line from S can reach.

2.1: Position S first, then press Fire (or Space) to test the current target.
2.2: For a target above the bar, raise S so the ray dips down past the top of the bar. For a target below the bar, lower S so the ray climbs past the bottom.
2.3: Check the boundary Sy: set y_hit = 175 (top) or 275 (bottom) and solve for Sy. Move to just past that boundary.

3.1: Read Sx, Tx, Ty, and the bar coordinates from the scene. Then Sy is your only unknown.
3.2: The ray S→T reaches x = 400 at y_hit = Sy + (400 − Sx)/(Tx − Sx) · (Ty − Sy). Solve for Sy so y_hit lands outside [175, 275].
3.3: Set y_hit at the bar edge (175 or 275) to find the critical Sy, then nudge past. Use Peek to confirm your Sy matches the sim.
